name: No-Peek Pork Chop and Rice Casserole
writer_notes: SELECTOR: Source verified at 415 cal / 26g protein per serving over 4 servings; scaling the chop weight up gets us past 500 cal at 30g+. Five pantry ingredients, all board-tracked (onion-soup-mix and cream-of-mushroom-soup included), dump-and-bake, and the rice cooks in the dish. Distinct from the live Southern Smothered Pork Chops and Rice (baked casserole, not stovetop gravy). | HARVEST: Published figures 414.8 calories and 25.8g protein per serving; rounded.
intro_html: The name is the instruction. You dump five things into a pan, cover it with foil, and you do not lift that foil until the timer goes off. The rice cooks in the beef broth and the cream of mushroom soup, taking on everything that drips off the chops above it, and the whole thing steams into a casserole with no stirring and no watching. Five ingredients. About ten minutes of actual work. Some recipes earn their keep by being clever and some earn it by being easy.
ingredients_display: Cream of Mushroom Soup (Campbell's (USDA SR)): 3.5 cans (1043 g)
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Cream of Mushroom Soup, 3.5 cans: ~$2.59. Buy 4 10.5oz cans: $2.96.
Beef Broth, 7 cups: ~$2.26. Pantry staple; this batch alone uses about 2 32oz cartons.
Onion Soup Mix, 3.5 oz: ~$3.16. Pantry staple; this batch alone uses about 2 2.2oz 2ct boxes.
Pantry seasonings (garlic powder, onion powder, salt, black pepper): ~$0.28. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $26.52 across 14 servings, so roughly $1.89 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $29.35 across 14 servings, roughly $2.10 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $8.43 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $37.78. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About ${{cost_ps}} a bowl (at everyday cost) for a full pork chop and a serving of gravy-soaked rice. Five ingredients means five chances to overspend, and there are not many of those here.
shop_smart: Bone-in chops cost less and cook better here. The bone keeps the meat from drying out during a long covered bake, and it comes off the price per pound too.
Store brand condensed soup is the same soup. Buy the generic cream of mushroom by the four pack. Once it is baked into rice, nobody could pick out the label.
Regular long grain white rice, not instant. Instant rice costs several times more per serving and turns to paste under an hour of covered heat. Plain white rice is what this method was built for.
Onion soup mix is the entire seasoning. One envelope replaces a whole rack of jars. If you buy the box of packets rather than singles, it costs very little per batch.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the oven to 350F and grease a large deep baking pan.
Stir the cream of mushroom soup together with the beef broth until smooth, then whisk in most of the onion soup mix.
Spread the uncooked rice evenly across the bottom of the pan and pour the soup mixture over it. Shake the pan flat, do not stir.
Season the pork chops with garlic powder, onion powder, salt and black pepper, and lay them across the top of the rice in a single layer.
Sprinkle the last of the onion soup mix over the chops, cover the pan tightly with foil, and get a good seal. Steam is what cooks the rice.
Bake for about 90 minutes without lifting the foil once, then rest 10 minutes before you uncover it.
portion_html: Weigh the finished casserole in its pan, subtract the pan weight, divide by 14, and portion to that exact weight so everybody gets chop and rice in the same ratio. Every serving lands near {{cal}} calories with {{protein}} grams of protein.

head.description: Pork chops baked over rice in cream of mushroom soup and beef broth under sealed foil. A five ingredient 14 serving casserole built for cheap meal prep.
head.keywords: no peek pork chops, pork chop rice casserole, dump and bake dinner, cream of mushroom recipe, budget meal prep, cheap dinner
recipeIngredient: Cream of Mushroom Soup, 3.5 cans (1043 g)
steps: Heat the oven to 350F and grease a large deep pan.
Stir the cream of mushroom soup with the beef broth and most of the onion soup mix.
Spread the uncooked rice in the pan and pour the soup mixture over it.
Season the pork chops, lay them on top, and sprinkle the remaining soup mix over.
Cover tightly with foil and bake 90 minutes without lifting the foil.
